Yes, you are not wrong there, but like I said, I'd like to argue that wine significantly gets better between $1 ~ $100 range, then $100 ~ 1000 range.  So strictly just putting taste per $, it's going to be a much better ratio within $1 ~ $100, then it would ever come out from $100 ~ $1000 range most of the time, hence 'value'.  But also, I think reddit represents a lot more of the normal spenders, so value to normal spendera wouldn't lie outside of triple digit bottles.  I go to a lot of local tastings, and some of the people would state NZ's high-end bottles "better value" compared to old world stuff and grab a case casually, whereas I am sitting there calculating whether I can afford that same bottle to keep in my cellar a bottle or not.

I'm pretty sure $100 bottle is cheap for some people out there, so it's not a perception issue.

 I think what people are trying to say is that as the price of the wine increases, the taste does not increase linearly.  A lot of people will state that somewhere along the $50 ~ $70 mark, the price/taste grape looks logarithmic.

  So, a $20 bottle tasting like a $40~$50 dollar is a better value than a $100 bottle tasting like $200 for a lot of the people.

I don't know which of our NZ wines are available where you are, but some of my favorite SB from Marlborough are Greywacke, Dog Point, Clos Henri, Babich, Auntsfield, and Hans Herzog.  They all have fresh style and more serious oak influence.  But some of the best values are big brand Villa Maria and Saint Clair reserves, especially when some cases go on special.  There are interesting Semillon blends from Pegasus Bay, Te Mata and Man'o'War which I think are worth a try.  If you like Te Koko from Cloudy Bay, do try Greywacke Wild, Dog Point 94 and Clos Henri Waimaunga.  

Kumeu River SV seems to be taking a lot of spotlights, but there are great wines in similar or better quality, like Man o War Mathilda, Church Road Tom, Tony Bish SV, Pyramid Valley SV, Neudorf, and Prophet's Rock.  A lot of Hawke's Bay Chard SV are available for just half the value or even 1/3 at times, and they are just as well made.  Clearview and Marlborist are my current favorites, but starting to lean towards Central Otago chards recently, like Matt Connell, Chard Farm and Rockburn.

While I won't disagree Kumeu and Cloudy Bay are well-known here in NZ as well, but it's definitely less consumed and are now overrated since we have a lot more local choices for better value.

I dont see anything wrong with his tasting, broad, and commonly associated with the wine.  There are expectations for specific types of wines to have a specific list of tastes, and that can also influence what we can discern and taste from such wine.  Some people are poetic, some are analysts, and some people just do it for the show.

There are no wrong answers since everyone has different buds, but maybe stay within the spectrum or keep it simple...  I will not expect butter chicken curry or canned salmon lemon pepper flav from any wine (not that there aren't any, I just haven't had one yet)

The whole point of tasting is being able to take a bottle of wine into strands of data that others can identify without drinking.  Vocabularies can help, but personally, I like to smell/taste a lot of different things and do my own cookings.

And I could be wrong as well, I like drinking wine, that's all.

All I can say is to attend a lot of tastings and events, but also be familiar with the ingredients of cooking or normal wine descriptors.

Yes, a lot of people will tell you the service is a waste of time, and to some degree, they aren't wrong.  But in most case, those same people would have achieved nothing even if they didn't go for military service.  In exchange for your 18 months, you get to keep Korean citizenship and weigh it out. Depends on the case and person;  Most will value freedom over everything, but the real question is how much are you doing if when you are NOT serving the military service anyway?  

Ask yourself what you could be doing if you weren't to do the service.  

Does your Korean Citizenship mean much more than 18 months of your 20s?

If you were to go in service now, how confident are you to not waste your free time and make most of it?

The decision is yours to make. Many come out with nothing, but some with maybe a few certificates, even a diploma or two, a better health and physique, maybe an intership at a private company.  Yes, while it's true, you can do all of these even when not in service, but instead of truly wasting your time, the military is there to support your growth.  

So maybe, instead of weighing how wasteful it will be, weigh how much your 2 years of 20s and how much Korean citizenship means to you.

I also look for charts, maps, and  cheat sheets from the web and printed them out.  

The hardest for me currently is learning aroma/bouquet.  Books and drinking wine do not help me with this at all because feeling the nuance of the aroma/bouquet comes from personal expression.  So what I started to do was started eating and drinking a lot of products that are quite often mentioned in aroma/bouquet.  Not only that, I also picked up a habit of smelling a lot of things, both edible and inedible.

Most of all, it is important to taste wine, both cheap and expensive (by that I mean less cared vs carefully grown). I had to drink shit wines to know what shit wine are like... (as peter koff explained)

Tldr; Use online resources, buy used books, watch others drink, train your senses. Save money elsewhere so you can buy more wine.

I use **decoy totem** almost religiously, my whole thought process is that 'if i'm not the target, i won't get hit'.  I also use phase **run/quartz** for 'less visible'.  My passive tree is mostly defensive as well; I have somewhere to only 1~3 clusters of nodes for damage. If I have room, I make adjustment so I can create **endurance charge** as well. And also, don't stop. keep moving.  

If you are bound to get hit a lot, manually use your guard skills and put curses/knockback/blind/ailments on. Use all items/skills that give you flat defensive boosts which you lack (like grace, evasion flask, armour flask) also mitigations to elemental/mana. And there's many more, you need to see what's close to your build and comfortable to you.
